(Per Hon'ble Dr.SA,J) Tanniru Bhramaiah, S/o.

Tanniru Subbaiah, the petitioner, has filed the present Habeas Corpus petition, on behalf of his son, Tanneru Venkateshwarlu @ Venkat @ Nepal,
in order to challenge the detention order, dated 06.06.2020, passed by the Commissioner of Police,
Hyderabad City, Hyderabad, respondent No.2, and the consequential confirmation order, dated 19.10.2020, passed by the State of Telangana, through General Administration (Spl. (Law and Order)) Department, represented by its Principal Secretary, Hyderabad, respondent No.1.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for both sides and perused the record.

3. The petitioner submits that on 06.06.2020, respondent No.2 passed the impugned detention order on the ground that the detenu committed burglaries in the limits of Hyderabad and Warangal Police Commissionerates and in Nalgonda District and that he is a 'Goonda' as defined in Clause (g)
of Section 2 of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits,
Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders,
Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders,
Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders,
Explosive Substances Offenders, ARR,J & Dr.SAJ Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short, 'the Act') and cases in Crime No.378 of 2019 of SR Nagar Police Station, Hyderabad City, was registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under Sections 457 and 380 I.P.C. and Crime No.287 of 2019 of Chityal Police Station,
Nalgonda District, Crime Nos.230 and 231 of 2019 of Kazipet Police Station, Warangal Commissionerate, were registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under Sections 454 and 380 I.P.C.
4.

The four criminal cases registered against the detenu cannot be termed as disturbance to public order.
The copy of bail order granted in Crime No.287 of 2019 of Chityal Police Station, Nalgonda District, was not served on the detenu along with the impugned detention order.

The detaining authority was of the apprehension that since the detenu was released on bail in the aforesaid four criminal cases,

sentences.text: The impugned detention order is passed on assumptions and presumptions.
The detaining authority, without there being any fresh crime registered against the detenu, after his release on bail in the aforesaid crimes, passed the impugned detention order.
The ordinary law was already invoked against the detenu to curb his ARR,J & Dr.SAJ illegal activities and invoking the preventive detention law, as an alternative method, is abuse of process of law.
The impugned detention order and the consequential confirmation order are unsustainable and the same are liable to be set aside.

5. On the other hand, Sri K.Srikanth Reddy, learned Government Pleader for Home, appearing on behalf of the learned Advocate General, would submit that the detenu involved in several cases covered by Chapter Nos.XVI, XVII and XXII of I.P.C.

As the activities of the detenu were prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, during the year 2015, he was detained vide proceedings SB(I)
No.471/PD/S-1/2015, dated 19.08.2015, and after completion of the detention period, he was released from jail.

Thereafter, in the year 2019, he committed four house burglaries, which demonstrates his habitual nature of committing crime, creating large scale fear in the public, apart from disturbing the peace and tranquility in the society.

The impugned detention order, grounds of detention and the documents relied upon by the detaining authority were served on the detenu in English as well as in the mother tongue of the detenu i.e., Telugu within the statutory period under acknowledgment.

Though a copy of the bail order passed in Crime No.287 of 2019 was not served on the detenu, copies of the bail petition and the release order in the said crime were served on him and he acknowledged the receipt of the same.
Moreover, the detenu is well aware of the said facts and no prejudice would be caused to him due to non-supply of a copy of the bail order in Crime No.287 of 2019.

The detaining authority considering the facts that since 2002 the detenu has involved in ARR,J & Dr.SAJ several cases; that in the year 2015, detention order was passed against him; that the cases registered against him under the ordinary law had no deterrent effect in curbing his prejudicial activities, and that he was already granted bail in all the cases and that there is every possibility of he indulging in similar prejudicial activities, passed the impugned detention order in the interest of public at large.
Further, all the aforesaid crimes were registered against the detenu for the offences punishable under Sections 454, 457 and 380 I.P.C. covered by Chapter No.XVII I.P.C.
Hence, the detenu comes under the expression 'Goonda'.
The detenu is a habitual offender committing series of offences in the limits of Hyderabad and Warangal Police Commissionerate and in Nalgonda District.
The case of the detenu was referred to the Advisory Board.

After hearing the detenu and the investigating officer, the Advisory Board rendered its report/opinion, whereby and whereunder, the Advisory Board opined that there is sufficient cause for detention of the detenu.

The Government, upon receipt of the report/opinion from the Advisory Board and upon considering the entire material, independently, confirmed the detention of the detenu vide order, dated 19.10.2020.
6.

In view of the submissions made by both the sides, the point that arises for determination in this Writ Petition is:
"Whether the detention order, dated 06.06.2020, passed by respondent No.2 and the consequential confirmation order, dated 19.10.2020, passed by respondent No.1 are Tanniru Bhramaiah vs The State Of Telangana And Another on 25 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101194049/

sentences.text:
ARR,J & Dr.SAJ POINT:
7.
In catena of cases, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had clearly opined that there is a vast difference between "law and order" and "public order".
The offences which are committed against a particular individual fall within the ambit of "law and order".
It is only when the public at large is adversely affected by the criminal activities of a person, the conduct of a person is said to disturb the public order.
Moreover, individual cases can be dealt with by the criminal justice system.
Therefore, there is no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention laws against an individual.
For the invoking of such law adversely effects the fundamental right of personal liberty which is protected and promoted by Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
Hence, according to the Honourable Apex Court, the detaining authority should be wary of invoking the immense power under the Act.

8. In the case of Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Honourable Supreme Court has, in fact,
deprecated the invoking of the preventive law in order to tackle a law and order problem.

entities.text: Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as under:
"54.

We have here a case of detention under Rule 30 of the Defence of India Rules which permits apprehension and detention of a person likely to act in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
It follows that if such a person is not detained public disorder is the apprehended result.

Disorder is no doubt prevented by the maintenance of law and order also but disorder is a broad spectrum which AIR 1966 SC 740 ARR,J & Dr.SAJ includes at one end small disturbances and at the other the most serious and cataclysmic happenings.
Does the expression "public order' take in every kind of disorders or only some of them?
The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them.
Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder.
Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder.
When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder.
They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order.
Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions.
The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder.
Other examples can be imagined.
The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large.
A mere disturbance of law and order leading to disorder is thus not necessarily sufficient for action under the Defence of India Act but disturbances which subvert the public order are.
A District Magistrate is entitled to take action under Rule 30(1)(b) to prevent subversion of public order but not in aid of maintenance of law and order under ordinary circumstances."

In the case of Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2, the Honourable Supreme Court has opined as under:
"The question whether a man has only committed a breach of law and order or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the public order is a question of degree and the extent of the (1972) 3 SCC 831 ARR,J & Dr.SAJ reach of the act upon the society.

entities.text: Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Public order is what the French call 'order publique' and is something more than ordinary maintenance of law and order.

The test to be adopted in determining whether an act affects law and order or public order, as laid down in the above case, is: Does it lead to disturbance of the current of life of the community so as to amount to a disturbance of the public order or does it affect merely an individual leaving the tranquility of the society undisturbed?"
10.

Grave as the offence may be, it has been committed against particular individuals.

So, no inference of disturbance of ARR,J & Dr.SAJ public order can be Tanniru Bhramaiah vs The State Of Telangana And Another on 25 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101194049/

sentences.text: The instant case can be tried under the normal criminal law.
The detenu was released on bail on 06.01.2020.
As per the submissions made on behalf of the detenu, after release, he has not involved in any crime or criminal activity.
The detention order was passed on 06.06.2020 i.e., about five months after the release of the detenu from prison.
There are no attempts or commission of the offences of the nature for which the detenu is being prosecuted.
As per the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner/detenu, bail was granted on certain conditions and those conditions were not violated by the detenu.
The conditions are not referred to in the impugned detention order.
Under these circumstances, there was no need for the detaining authority to pass the detention order.
The impugned detention order, dated 06.06.2020, suffers from non-application of mind.
[Ref. to Rekha v. State of Tamil Nadu through Secretary to Government & another3].

dated 19.10.2020, passed by respondent No.1 are hereby set aside.
The respondents are directed to set the detenu, namely Tanneru Venkateshwarlu @ Venkat @ Nepal, S/o. Bhramaiah, at liberty forthwith, if he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
